outcome: Change in hematocrit pre- and post-delivery
cohort: Pregnant women with singleton or twin pregnancies, including very preterm, moderate preterm, late preterm, and term pregnancies. The study also included women undergoing cesarean section.
finding: Delayed cord clamping (DCC) or umbilical cord milking (UCM) was not associated with an increased risk for PPH or significant change in maternal hematocrit pre- and post-delivery in various preterm and term delivery scenarios.
mod_finding: This study found that delayed cord clamping (DCC) or umbilical cord milking (UCM) was not associated with an increased risk for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in preterm singleton, moderate preterm, very preterm twin gestation, late preterm, and term cesarean deliveries.
gest_age: Very preterm, moderate preterm, late preterm (32-36 weeks gestation), and term
